title: Content Addressed Knowledge Graph
definition: A decentralized, open-source network for storing, sharing, and discovering knowledge, structured as a graph where nodes represent concepts and edges represent relationships.

difficulty_levels.beginner: A digital library where every idea is given a unique address, like a digital fingerprint. This allows for easy organization, sharing, and discovery of knowledge.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A knowledge graph that uses content-addressing to ensure decentralization and openness, with each concept represented as a node and relationships between concepts represented as edges.
difficulty_levels.expert: A philosophical exploration of knowledge representation and organization, leveraging content-addressing for decentralization and openness, creating a network of interconnected concepts and relationships that evolves with the collective intelligence of its users.

extra_fields.insight: Decentralized, open-source knowledge networks allow for the democratization of knowledge, enabling collaborative intelligence and continuous learning.
